title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Specific Provisions on the Forced Sale of Detained Ships to Satisfy Debts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Specific Provisions on Compulsory Sale of Arrested Ships to Pay Off Debts

Fa (Jing) Fa [1987] No. 22

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and all Maritime Courts:

We hereby issue the Specific Provisions on Compulsory Sale of Arrested Ships to Pay Off Debts to your courts for conscientious implementation.

August 29, 1987

Supreme People's Court

Specific Provisions on Compulsory Sale of Arrested Ships to Pay Off Debts

In accordance with the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), on the basis of summing up trial experience, and with reference to customary international practices, the specific provisions on compulsory sale of arrested ships to pay off debts are as follows:

I. Compulsory Sale of a Ship

(1) If, within 30 days after the arrest of a ship, the shipowner refuses to provide sufficient and reliable security, or the cost of keeping the ship under custody is substantial, or the ship itself or its machinery or equipment are unsuitable for continued arrest, the court may, upon the applicant's application, order a compulsory sale of the ship.

(2) An applicant applying for a compulsory sale of a ship shall file an action with the court that arrested the ship and submit a written application for compulsory sale of the ship.

(3) After receiving the application for compulsory sale of the ship, the court accepting the case shall examine whether the application has sufficient reasons and basis, and promptly render a ruling approving or disapproving the compulsory sale. The ruling must be approved by the president of the court.

If the respondent or the applicant objects to the ruling, either party may apply for reconsideration once.

(4) If losses are caused by an erroneous application, the applicant shall be liable for compensation. All expenses during the period of the sale of the ship shall be advanced by the applicant.

(5) After the court accepting the case rules to compulsorily sell the arrested ship, it shall publish a notice of the sale of the ship in China Daily and People's Daily (domestic and overseas editions) on three consecutive days. The notice shall include the following:

1. The reasons and basis for the sale of the ship;

2. The establishment of a Ship Sale Committee responsible for the sale of the ship;

3. The conditions for prospective buyers and the method for obtaining ship particulars and inspecting the ship's current condition;

4. The method, time, place, and contact information for the sale;

5. Creditors with claims relating to the ship shall register their claims with the court accepting the case within 60 days from the date of the notice; failure to register within the time limit shall be deemed as waiving the right to receive payment in this sale.

(6) The Sale Committee shall be composed of three to five persons, including a court bailiff, an accountant, and a marine surveyor, designated by the court accepting the case. The tasks of the Sale Committee are: to organize the appraisal and valuation of the ship; to preside over the sale and to sign a confirmation of sale with the buyer; after the sale is concluded, to handle the transfer of the ship, sign a confirmation of completion of ship transfer, and issue a certificate of transfer of ownership of the ship.

(7) A creditor registering a claim shall submit a written application and evidence supporting the claim. After examination, if the court accepting the case considers the registration conditions are met, it shall issue a notice of acceptance of the application. Upon receipt of the notice, the applicant shall submit a certificate of legal representative status and a power of attorney to the agent ad litem to the court, and pay a registration fee of RMB 500.

(8) A prospective buyer shall register with the Sale Committee within the prescribed period and, prior to the sale, submit identification of the buyer or the legal representative of the enterprise, a power of attorney to the agent ad litem, and a bank certificate evidencing the ability to pay in foreign currency.

(9) The reserve price of the ship to be sold shall be determined by the court accepting the case. The reserve price shall not be disclosed.

(10) The sale of the ship shall be conducted by public auction, and the sale shall be concluded to the highest bidder above the reserve price. If the bids are below the reserve price, a second public auction may be held, or the ship may be sold by other means.

(11) After the sale is concluded, the Sale Committee shall sign a confirmation of sale with the buyer. The buyer shall pay a deposit of 20-25% of the purchase price immediately, and pay the full price within seven days from the day following the conclusion of the sale. If the buyer reneges, the deposit shall not be refunded. The proceeds from the sale and the interest shall be used together for the payment of debts.

(12) Within five days from the day following the buyer's full payment of the purchase price, the Sale Committee shall, at the place where the ship is moored, transfer the ship in its condition as sold, sign a confirmation of completion of ship transfer with the buyer, and issue a certificate of transfer of ownership of the ship.

(13) At the same time as the transfer of the ship, the court shall issue an order to release the ship from arrest.

(14) After the compulsory sale of the ship is concluded, the court accepting the case shall publish a notice in the aforementioned newspapers stating that the ship has been sold by public auction by the Sale Committee to the buyer, that the ownership of the ship has been transferred from the time of transfer, that the buyer assumes no liability for any debts of the ship incurred prior to the transfer, and that the original shipowner shall voluntarily apply for deregistration with the original registration authority.

II. After the compulsory sale of the ship, the court accepting the case shall promptly hear the action filed, determine the creditor's claim and its amount, and determine that such claim, together with the claims of other creditors, shall be satisfied from the proceeds of the ship sale in accordance with the order of priority and on a pro rata basis.

III. Settlement of Debts

(1) After the expiration of the period for registration of claims, the court accepting the case shall convene a meeting of creditors. All creditors shall, through consultation, propose a plan for the distribution of the proceeds from the ship sale in accordance with the order of priority, and sign a settlement agreement, which shall be approved by a ruling of the court accepting the case. If consultation fails, the court accepting the case shall render a ruling.

(2) Order of priority. The order of priority for payment of claims is as follows:

1. Claims for compensation arising from personal injury or death in the course of ship operations, and claims of the master and other crew members serving on board for overdue wages under labor law or labor contracts;

2. State taxes, harbor dues, and other port charges;

3. Salvage awards and general average contributions;

4. Claims for compensation arising from ship collisions or other maritime accidents, including claims for compensation arising from damage to docks, navigational aids, or other port installations or facilities in connection with the operation of the ship;

5. Other registered claims.

If a ship mortgage overlaps with the above claims, its priority for payment shall be after the claims under item 4 and before the claims under item 5. If there are several mortgages, they shall be satisfied in the order in which they were created.

Claims within the same priority rank shall be satisfied in proportion, without priority; however, for claims under item 3, a later-arising claim shall have priority; several claims arising from the same incident shall be deemed to have arisen at the same time.

However, before payment according to the above order, court costs, expenses incurred for the common benefit of the creditors, and all expenses incurred in the compulsory sale of the ship shall be deducted first.

(3) Any surplus remaining after settlement of debts shall be returned to the defendant.

IV. If a ship is sold after a judgment or arbitral award has become legally effective, the above provisions may be applied by reference.
